definition: Cogent means intellectually convincing; clearly reasoned.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word cogent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know cogent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The registrar's memo was so cogent that the dean approved the new major before her coffee had cooled.
Convincing is a broader, weaker rung than cogent — a slogan or a single statistic can be convincing without much rigor, while a cogent case compels agreement through the reasoning itself.
Irrefutable goes further than cogent — a cogent case compels agreement, but an irrefutable one cannot even be argued against.

A sound argument simply contains no errors — the logic holds and the facts check out — but sound is a pass mark, not a wow. A cogent argument is sound and forceful at once: it does not just survive inspection, it compels agreement. Many sound arguments persuade no one; a cogent one wins the room.

Airtight is the informal word for a case with no gap for an objection to slip through — it stresses the absence of holes. Cogent stresses the positive push: reasoning so clear and well-ordered that it moves you to agree. An airtight case cannot be beaten; a cogent one wins you over.

The school board had heard four years of complaints about the 7:10 start time and moved on every time.
Then Priya Raman, a junior, took the podium with a folder and a stopwatch.
Her case was cogent in a way the complaints had never been: sleep data first, then bus schedules, then a cost table, each point built on the one before, each objection answered before it was raised.
Board members later admitted they had arrived intending to say no.
